text: Aijaz Ahmad Khan, popularly known as Sher-e-Gool Gulabgarh, is an Indian politician who served as a member of the 10th, 11th, and 12th Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly from the Gool Arnas constituency. He held various ministerial portfolios from 2002 to 2014 in the Jammu and Kashmir government under the chief ministership of Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, Ghulam Nabi Azad, and Omar Abdullah. He also served as Deputy Leader of the Congress Legislative Party from 2014 to 2018. In March 2020, he left the Indian National Congress and became a founding member of the Jammu and Kashmir Apni Party (JKAP), which was formed on 8 March 2020. He held the position of Vice President of the Political Affairs Committee (PAC) and member of the Central Working Committee (CWC) of JKAP. Prior to the Jammu and Kashmir 2024 Assembly Elections, Khan exited the Apni Party and contested as an independent candidate from the Gulabgarh Assembly constituency, where he secured a runner-up position and lost the election. Currently, he is the patron of the Gujjar Bakerwal Conference (GBC), a social and political platform founded in 2000 by his father, Haji Buland Khan, a veteran leader, who played a crucial role in the upliftment of the Gujjar Bakerwal community. Ajaz Ahmad Khan was born on 21 November 1968 in Thuroo, Dharmari, Jammu & Kashmir, to Haji Buland Khan, a renowned Gujjar leader who held various posts in the state government. He completed his early schooling at Govt. High School, Thuroo, Reasi, and earned his B.A. from Jammu University, Jammu. In 1996, he completed his LLB from Jammu University. He married Farhat Un Nisa Khan in 2003. His younger brother, Haji Mumtaz Ahmad Khan, was also a member of the 12th Jammu and Kashmir Legislative Assembly from the Gulabgarh constituency. One of his sisters is married to Chowdhary Zulfikar Ali. Ajaz joined politics in 1996, shortly after completing his LLB, and contested the elections on the ticket of the National Conference (NC) from Gulabgarh, where he lost by a margin of 956 votes. He was then appointed District President of NC for Reasi District (Udhampur II). In 2002, he contested as an independent candidate from two assembly segments—Gool Arnas and Gulabgarh—and won from Gool Arnas, after which he joined the Indian National Congress. He won from Gool Arnas in 2008 and 2014. He remained a minister from 2002 to 2014 in the governments of Mufti Mohammad Sayeed, Ghulam Nabi Azad, and Omar Abdullah, holding various departments, including charge of 13 departments at one point. In 2020, he co-founded the Jammu and Kashmir Apni Party with Altaf Bukhari. He is also the patron of the Gujjar Bakerwal Conference (GBC), established in 2000 by his father and veteran leader Haji Buland Khan, which has significantly contributed to the upliftment of the Gujjar Bakerwal community.
